title: The selected derived pullback/direct-image adjunction commutes with shifts
statement: The selected derived pullback/direct-image adjunction commutes with shifts. For chosen derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] and additive tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback], take any family of pullback integer shift comparisons compatible with the selected left-derived counits [lem-pc-pinned-pullback-counit-shifts]. For each morphism f, the adjunction selected by [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] with that counit has shift-compatible unit and counit, using the recorded direct-image shift structure.

source.place: The selected derived pullback/direct-image adjunction commutes with shifts; shift verification of the constructions, written by K4.

proof.text: Prove canonicalRightDerivedUnitShift: the inverse of rightDerivedFunctorIsoKInjectives is the right-derived unit on the representative followed by the image of the K-injective equivalence counit. Express the restriction of the right-derived unit using this inverse and the equivalence unit. All factors commute with the recorded shifts. Every complex has a K-injective resolution, so NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerLeft extends compatibility to the whole homotopy category.

Hold the recorded right-derived shift structure fixed and give derivedPullback the leftAdjointCommShift structure induced by pinnedDerivedAdjunction. Mathlib commShift_of_rightAdjoint makes this adjunction shift compatible. The termwise homotopy adjunction is shift compatible by commShift_mapHomotopyCategory_unit and Adjunction.CommShift.mk'.

Apply normalizedCounitShift to the Hom-equivalence equation supplied by Classical.choose_spec exists_schemeDerivedAdjunction. Evaluating at the identity identifies pinnedPullbackCounit with the inverse mate of the canonical right-derived unit. The inverse-mate formula uses only shift-compatible units, counits and whiskerings, hence pinnedPullbackCounit commutes with the adjunction-induced left shifts.

Apply rightKanShiftUnique to the specified left-derived counit, which is a right Kan extension counit. Postcomposition with any integer shift preserves its universal property because shift is an equivalence. The two shift comparisons have the same composite with the shifted counit by their NatTrans.CommShift equations; Kan hom_ext identifies them. Thus the supplied s f equals the induced left shift structure. Transport commShift_of_rightAdjoint across this equality to obtain the claimed compatibility with the original s f and the recorded right-derived shifts.

proof_origin.place: Canonical derived adjunction normalization; K-injective transport, the inverse-mate formula and uniqueness of counit-compatible shifts under the left-derived universal property. Lean proof by Q3.

theorem pinnedDerivedAdjunction_commShift
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (k : Y ⟶ Z), (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback k).Additive]
    (s : ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y), (derivedPullback.{u, w} f).CommShift ℤ)
    (hs : ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y),
      letI := s f
      NatTrans.CommShift (pinnedPullbackCounit.{u, w} f) ℤ)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    letI := s f
    (pinnedDerivedAdjunction.{u, w} f).CommShift ℤ
